item.description: 25 years ago, Tom Brokaw delivered an NBC News Special Report on September 11, 2001, after terrorists hijacked four commercial planes and carried out coordinated attacks against targets in the U.S. Two were flown into the World Trade Center's Twin Towers, one into the Pentagon, and one – after the passengers and crew fought back – crashed into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing nearly 3,000 people.

item.description: Former FDNY paramedic Roger Smyth shares his photographs taken on September 11, and reflects on partnering with FDNY paramedic Trinh K. Dinh, to care for survivors after both got separated from their regular partners. He also captured the moments Trinh and her partner, Ronnie Coyne, reunited after Ronnie was thought to be lost in the collapse at Ground Zero. Roger’s partner also survived the chaos at Ground Zero.

item.description: Olivia Perez-Johntry was just 10 years old when she lost her father on 9/11. Now 25 years later, she has turned that loss into lessons of resiliency as a high school science teacher on Long Island, New York. She sits down with TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to open up about how she dealt with the unimaginable loss and is using her own experience to help others.

item.description: Elizabeth Holmes was a single mother working at the World Trade Center when the unthinkable happened on 9/11. Her son, Reverend Travis Boyd, is now preserving her legacy with his book “The Purse She Left Behind.” He talks about the significance of her purse, his relationship with Reverend Al Sharpton, and how he has dealt with the immeasurable loss. “My story isn’t defined by tragedy, it’s defined by the vision my mother had for me,” he says.

media:content.media:title: Son of 9/11 Victim Honors Mother's Legacy With New Book

item.description: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has created a special half dollar to be given to the families of 9/11 victims. The coin features the Statue of Liberty and the inscription “Always Remember 9-11-01” as well as a “W” to represent West Point, where the coins were minted by New Yorkers. They will be distributed around the nation.
